newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Key Nigerian oil refinery reopens after clashes.
newsitem.headline: Key Nigerian oil refinery reopens after clashes.

text.p: Nigeria's Warri refinery reopened on Tuesday after being closed for days because of ethnic clashes, an official of the state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) said.
Restarting the refinery is expected to end panic buying of fuel by motorists who have thronged petrol stations since Monday to fill up in anticipation of fuel shortages.
"The Warri refinery is now fully operational," Yemi Dare, spokesman for the Pipelines and Products Marketing Company (PPMC), a subsidiary of the NNPC, told reporters in Lagos.
The 125,000 barrels per day (bpd) plant was shut down last week after its storage tanks were full and vessels were unable to sail into Warri to load products because of ethnic clashes in the area.
"The Nigerian navy have now provided escorts for vessels moving products from the refinery," Dare said.
The MT African Pride ship, which loaded 5,224 metric tonnes of gasoline was given a security escort to Lagos, he said.
Armed youths of the rival Ijaw and Itshekiri tribes had made waterways and major highways in the area unsafe following bloody clashes over the relocation of a local government headquarters.
Soldiers moved into the area last week to restore order.
